themes_detail.label: Illegal Tree Damage Spike
themes_detail.summary: Tree damage complaints surged to 11 THIS WEEK, a 418% spike above the 8-week average of 2.1 per week, suggesting either environmental damage, construction activity, or deliberate vandalism requiring urgent investigation.
evidence: 11 illegal tree damage complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (418% increase, z-score: 7.61)
Concentrated spike suggests common cause rather than random incidents
Active development pipeline (676 DOB permits filed in last 90 days, including 104 new buildings and 43 demolitions) may be contributing factor
reporting_angles: Are construction crews violating tree protection regulations during ongoing development projects?
Is there a storm or environmental event damaging trees, and are residents reporting it?

themes_detail.label: For Hire Vehicle Complaint Wave
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints jumped to 20 THIS WEEK, a 290% spike from the 8-week average of 5.1 per week, indicating emerging conflicts between Astoria residents and rideshare/livery services.
evidence: 20 for-hire vehicle complaints THIS WEEK vs. 5.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (290% increase, z-score: 4.51)
Spike emerges as multiple active rezonings (33-01 11th Street, 43-02 Ditmars Boulevard) may be attracting new commercial activity and traffic
Complements long-standing illegal parking crisis (6,240 complaints over 90 days)
reporting_angles: Are Uber/Lyft drivers congregating in specific neighborhoods while waiting for pickups?
Do new development projects lack adequate TLC vehicle parking or loading zones?

themes_detail.label: Outdoor Dining Infrastructure Complaints
themes_detail.summary: Outdoor dining complaints exploded to 4 THIS WEEK, a 540% spike from the 8-week baseline of 0.6 per week, suggesting either rapid expansion of sidewalk dining or resident backlash against existing installations.
evidence: 4 outdoor dining complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (540% increase, z-score: 6.97)
Timing aligns with warmer weather and potential post-pandemic dining expansion
Limited baseline complaints suggest this is genuinely emerging rather than chronic issue
reporting_angles: Are restaurants installing new or expanded outdoor seating without proper permits?
Are residents complaining about noise, blocked sidewalks, or other quality-of-life impacts from dining sheds?

themes_detail.label: Sanitation Worker Conduct Issues
themes_detail.summary: Sanitation worker and vehicle complaints spiked to 6 LAST WEEK, a 380% increase from the 8-week average of 1.2 per week, indicating potential service disruption or worker conduct problems in the district.
evidence: 6 sanitation worker complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (380% increase, z-score: 10.97)
Highest z-score among all spikes suggests statistically severe anomaly
Complements ongoing 'dirty condition' complaints (574 over 90 days)
reporting_angles: Has staffing shortage or scheduling change disrupted garbage collection in specific neighborhoods?
Are residents reporting unprofessional behavior or missed pickups by sanitation workers?

themes_detail.label: Water Quality Alert
themes_detail.summary: Water quality complaints hit 7 complaints TWO WEEKS AGO, a 2700% spike from the 8-week average of 0.2 per week, representing the most extreme statistical anomaly in the dataset.
evidence: 7 water quality complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (2700% increase, z-score: 10.21)
Second-highest z-score in dataset indicates extreme deviation
Community board repeatedly requests DOE and DEP capital funding, suggesting persistent infrastructure concerns
HEAT/HOT WATER remains high-volume complaint category (1,710 over 90 days)
reporting_angles: Was there a documented water main break, contamination event, or DEP advisory two weeks ago?
Are residents experiencing discolored water, low pressure, or other service issues affecting health or daily life?
